recommendation: Keep the commit as a targeted source clarification. If the work group later wants DetectedIssue to carry a typed FHIR Reference to ClinicalUseDefinition instead of the existing URI authority element, that should be handled as a separate substantive tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-21633 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request asking that DetectedIssue be distinguished from the then-new definitional ClinicalUseIssue resource, now ClinicalUseDefinition, and that DetectedIssue may point to that definitional issue for a particular patient case.
initial_application: Commit 5a901eb667bfa6f88e04cdebad84c53f8758388f, merged in HL7/fhir#2834, updated source/detectedissue/detectedissue-introduction.xml to say DetectedIssue represents a patient-specific potential issue and that ClinicalUseDefinition is for general patient-independent knowledge. That applied the resource-boundary part of the request, but the DetectedIssue.reference element still did not explicitly name ClinicalUseDefinition.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists detectedissue and clinicalusedefinition as active current-build resources. Current DetectedIssue narrative already points readers to ClinicalUseDefinition for general knowledge, and DetectedIssue.reference is the existing URI authority element for literature, knowledge-base, or similar references. Corrected Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-21633-specific discussion or conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Added a comment to source/detectedissue/structuredefinition-DetectedIssue.xml on DetectedIssue.reference stating that it may identify a ClinicalUseDefinition describing the general issue being detected in the specific patient context. The change is a clarification only and does not alter cardinality, datatype, target profiles, or behavior.
source_changes: source/detectedissue/structuredefinition-DetectedIssue.xml: added a DetectedIssue.reference comment naming ClinicalUseDefinition as the definitional issue authority for a patient-specific detected issue.
